content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU serving queue growth detected for prod-cluster-eu-west (pool 'highmem-gpu'). Queue length = 5124, 94% requests throttled, autoscaler not adding nodes. Pager sent to oncall.
Eric: Oncall ack. I'll start digging. Any customer impact reported yet? @Julia-CS can you check top 5 customers? :wave:
Julia-CS: Seeing elevated 5xx rate in metrics and several customer error reports around 11:02 UTC. Two customers reported degraded completions and high latency via support channel.
Susan: Looking at pool metrics — node count steady at 24 (max configured) and autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts that fail with 'alloc failed: rate-limiter' and 'scale-loop-livelock' messages.
Mike: Noted. We had a config rollout ~04:30 UTC that tightened continuous batching parameters and reduced prefix_cache_shards from 8 -> 2 to reduce memory pressure. Could be related.
Deepa: If prefix cache shards dropped, miss rate could spike and force more KV cache refills which blow up latency and reduce throughput. Can you post recent cache hit/miss stats?
infra-bot: Recent metric snapshot (11:05 UTC): prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.21 (was 0.96 at 03:50), avg_token_latency: 320ms -> 980ms, pool_utilization: 0.98, pending_queue: 5124.
Eric: That hit rate is huge. Rolling back shards would be quick. But autoscaler livelock is preventing new nodes — looks like scale requests are being rate-limited by cloud quota backoff. I'll try manual scale while we fix config.
Mike: Also seeing high continuous_batching.max_batch_size reduced in the rollout from 64 -> 16. That reduces batching effectiveness for long-tail latencies. Combined with cache miss storm it explains throughput drop.
Eric: Manual scale command to add 6 nodes:
```
kubectl scale deployment/gpu-pool-highmem --replicas=30 -n redwood-serving
```
Executing... (may take ~2-3m)
Susan: FYI autoscaler logs show repeated: `error: cannotAllocate: insufficient gpu_quota` and `allocator: backoff 30s due to partial failures` — cloud provider hitting regional quota. Manual scale may also hit same.
Eric: Manual scale failed with `quotaExceeded`. Ok, plan B: trigger immediate rollback of the config rollout that changed prefix cache shards + batching params. Rolling back to commit `c4f9a2b`.
Mike: Rolling back config now:
```
kubectl set configmap serving-config -n redwood-serving --from-file=serving-config.yaml@/releases/c4f9a2b/serving-config.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deployment/gpu-serving -n redwood-serving
```
Mike: Rollout started at 11:12 UTC. Restarting routing proxies to flush stale routing caches.
infra-bot: Deploy initiated. New pods coming up. Pre-shutdown drain configured to 30s to avoid inflight failures.
Deepa: After rollback we should also increase prefix_cache_shards back to 8 and revert continuous_batching.max_batch_size to 64. Also temporarily increase per-request throttling to avoid queue starve.
Anna: From product perspective we need a timeline to share with customers. Please post a short impact note once we have stable metrics.
Julia-CS: Noted — I have templates ready. Waiting on stability check.
Eric: Monitoring... at 11:18 UTC prefix_cache_hit_rate climbed to 0.69, avg_token_latency down to 450ms, pending_queue reduced to 1800.
Susan: Autoscaler still in a backoff loop. However with reduced latency and better batching we should bring down utilization and allow autoscaler to recover itself. I'm going to flush autoscaler leader lock to break livelock.
Susan: Running leader reset:
```
curl -XPOST http://autoscaler.internal/reset-leader -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Susan: Leader reset acknowledged. Autoscaler health check passed.
infra-bot: Autoscaler logs: 'reconcile: scale up ok' at 11:22 UTC. New scale attempt queued.
Eric: New nodes provisioned and joining — node count now 27 at 11:24 UTC (partial). Pending_queue = 650.
Mike: Confirming config values now: prefix_cache_shards=8, continuous_batching.max_batch_size=64. Also bumped prefix_cache_ttl from 60s -> 120s temporarily.
Deepa: Added a temporary fallback policy in routing to serve traffic for heavy customers from a pinned smaller model variant (lower memory) to reduce GPU pressure.
Eric: Good. Customer impact: earlier errors for two customers — one had ~20% failed requests, the other saw 4x latency. Post-mitigation latest metrics show errors <1% and latency within SLO for most.
Julia-CS: Sent interim update to impacted customers at 11:33 UTC: "We've identified a regression in batching/cache config causing elevated latency; mitigation in progress, please reach out if you still see issues." 
Anna: Please include root cause and timeline in final postmortem. Also need to know what changed in the deployment pipeline that allowed this config to roll out without a canary.
Mike: Quick root cause summary: accidental config change rolled via a bulk configmap deploy that coalesced two unrelated changes: reduced prefix_cache_shards and lowered max_batch_size. The combined effect created a cache miss storm and reduced batching efficiency which amplified per-request latency and caused sustained high utilization. Autoscaler then hit cloud quota and entered a rate-limited reconcile loop (livelock) preventing immediate capacity increase.
Deepa: Action items (short):
- Revert config deployment process to require per-cluster canary + automated smoke tests that include prefix cache hit/miss and batching throughput checks. (owner: Mike)
- Add autoscaler health probe to break on repeated rate-limit errors and escalate earlier (owner: Susan)
- Add quota pre-check before large scale rollouts and an emergency capacity playbook (owner: Eric)
- Add regression alert: prefix_cache_hit_rate drop > 20% within 30m triggers page. (owner: Deepa)
- Postmortem writeup with timeline and customer impact (owner: Anna)
Eric: I'm handing over to Deepa for the night shift. System stable, but keep an eye on regional quota and autoscaler logs. Handoff: last_state=stable, pending_queue=120, prefix_cache_hit_rate=0.94.
Deepa: Took handoff at 11:40 UTC :wave:. Will monitor next 6 hours and keep rotating nodes at safe margins. If anything, I'll escalate to infra team.
Julia-CS: I'll follow up with customers once we confirm 2 hours of stable SLOs. Draft postmortem in #postmortems when ready.
incident-bot: Pager resolved by Eric at 11:41 UTC. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: Sev2. Link to temporary incident doc: https://confluence.internal/incidents/2009456789
Eric: Closing notes: Avoid combining cache and batching changes in single deploy, add canary checks. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
